name: Thymoma Type AB

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Thymic Epithelial Tumors

criteria.description: Presence of mixed lymphocyte-rich and spindle/oval epithelial cells in tumor tissue
Anterior mediastinal mass on chest CT or MRI consistent with thymic tumor
Positive staining for cytokeratins and immature T-cell markers (CD1a, TdT) in lymphocytic component

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of mixed lymphocyte-rich and spindle epithelial cells with supportive immunohistochemistry
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology, immunohistochemistry, and imaging findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anterior mediastinal mass detected on imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Often asymptomatic but detected incidentally or due to mass effect
searchTerms: mass in front of chest detected by scan
muscle weakness linked to myasthenia gravis
skeletal muscle weakness with fluctuating severity

common.symptomName: Dyspnea due to mass effect on airways
searchTerms: shortness of breath from airway compression
difficulty breathing due to mass pressing on airways

common.symptomName: Chest pain localized to anterior mediastinum
common.notes: Due to tumor invasion or inflammation
searchTerms: chest pain in front of chest
symptoms from blocked superior vena cava
swelling and breathing issues from vein obstruction
signs of superior vena cava blockage

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement
searchTerms: hoarse voice due to nerve involvement
unintentional weight loss and poor appetite
failure to produce red blood cells
pure red cell aplasia causing anemia

rare.symptomName: Superior phrenic nerve palsy causing diaphragmatic paralysis
searchTerms: phrenic nerve damage leading to breathing problems

laboratory: Elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies in cases with myasthenia gravis
Anemia with reticulocytopenia in pure red cell aplasia
imaging: Well-defined anterior mediastinal mass on chest CT or MRI
Calcifications within the tumor may be present
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; somatic mutations variable
other: Histopathology showing mixed lymphocyte-rich and spindle epithelial cells
Immunohistochemical positivity for cytokeratins and immature T-cell markers

distinguishingFeatures: More aggressive histology with cytologic atypia
Poor prognosis compared to thymoma type AB

redFlags: New onset or worsening myasthenic crisis
Signs of superior vena cava syndrome
references: Travis WD, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Lung, Pleura, Thymus and Heart. IARC; 2021.
Detterbeck FC, et al. The Masaoka-Koga stage classification for thymic malignancies. J Thorac Oncol. 2011.
Marx A, et al. The 2021 WHO classification of tumors of the thymus: Continuity and changes. J Thorac Oncol. 2022.
